subject: What is the ID in f(ID, model="bym", graph=LDN.adj) ?

messages.author: a72127847885c8e4
messages.subject: What is the ID in f(ID, model="bym", graph=LDN.adj) ?
parts:
Hello, everyone. I am a beginner using INLA.
Recently, I read this book to learn how to use it to do spatial-temporal analysis. 

In the book, there is a formula for spatial data modelling. 
formula <- y ~ 1 + f(ID, model="bym", graph=LDN.adj) 
As the book says, ID represents the identifiers for the area. 
How do I know which ID number represent certain area ? 

For example, The data I have is like 
place             y               ID 
Munich    3 cases           ?
Berlin      4 cases           ? 
and something like that ....

I also have the Germany.adj file and I can visualise adjacency matrix. 
How do I know which ID number represent Munich, Berlin ,... if the shape file doesn't give me any hins? 
 
Thank you for you guys help in advance.

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] What is the ID in f(ID, model="bym", graph=LDN.adj) ?

ID would be define the region. with a graph of size n, it will be one
of 1, 2, 3, ..., n.

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] What is the ID in f(ID, model="bym", graph=LDN.adj) ?
parts:
I just found out the solution. :) 
I overlooked the matrix that I converted from the file. 

Here is the code that I converted the shape file to adj file : 

library(maptools)
library(sf)
library(spdep)
Germany.gen <- readShapePoly("de_county.shp")
temp <- poly2nb(Germany.gen)
nb2INLA("Germany.graph", temp)
Germany.adj <- paste(getwd(),"/Germany.graph",sep="")

The information of the ID is stored in Germany.gen. 
I just need to code Germany.gen$GEN to read it.
